punchline: Output rose a third while the Depression raged, and almost nobody saw it.
thirty_sec: By 1932 almost a quarter of Americans had no job, yet economist Alexander Field argues the 1930s were the most technologically progressive decade of the century: R&D employment rose from 10,918 to 27,777 between 1933 and 1940, and by 1941 output was 33 to 40 percent above 1929 with about the same labour and capital.
question: What are you quietly building in your hardest stretch that nobody has counted yet?
key_contrast: The pain was loud and visible; the progress was slow and hidden.
